I was bound down by this disease of the flesh, he wrote.

sentences.en: Its deadly pleasures were a chain that I dragged along with me.

Aurelius happened to be one of the most prolific writers of his time,

sentences.en: so we have a detailed picture of his mind from his various books and writings.

那么，让我们回到杰姬的故事上来，她就是你那位多年来一直在与她所称的“渴望怪兽”作斗争的病人。
她发现好奇心和善意确实改变了她的饮食习惯。
贾德，给我讲讲她的故事吧。
从一个故事开始，这个故事很好地说明了这一点。我记得有位病人来到我的办公室，他说的第一句话是：“嘿，医生，如果我不抽烟，我的头都要炸了。”我当时心想，糟糕，医学院里可没教过这个，你知道的，主诉是“因不抽烟而头痛欲裂”，也就是因为渴望。所以我不得不临场发挥。当然，作为一名研究者和老师，我的习惯是走到白板前。
所以，你知道，我试着去问他到底发生了什么，他说他以前总是在渴望变得如此强烈之前就抽烟了，但这次渴望消退了，而他并没有抽烟。对他来说，这是一个巨大的“顿悟”时刻，他意识到这些渴望是由思想、感觉和情绪组成的，仅仅是给它们命名，甚至大声说出来，就能帮助他看清它们的本质。
在心理学中，这被称为“观察者效应”。通过观察我们的思想，我们就不再会同时认同它们。因此，这位病人是在观察他的思想和身体感觉，而不是被它们所吞噬或认同它们。
通过这样做，他意识到他并不是他的思想，并且通过简单地观察它们，他就获得了控制权。
他可以与自己的身体感觉共处，而不必去做些什么，比如抵抗渴望或抽烟。
你有另一位病人，你称他为 Rob Judd，你问 Rob 为什么会强迫性暴饮暴食，并要求他在强迫性暴饮暴食时密切关注自己的进食过程。

sentences.en: And you did this with gummy bears.
sentences.zh: 这可以追溯到20世纪70年代。

sentences.en: And this is what you do when you tell smokers to go ahead and smoke, but to pay very close attention to it.
sentences.zh: 这两位研究人员，Raskorla 和 Wagner，提出了这些强化学习模型。

sentences.en: And again, the idea is that paying very close attention to the eating of the food, to the smoking of the cigarette, to the drinking of the wine,
sentences.zh: 它们至今仍在发挥作用。

sentences.en: it changes your experience of the thing that you were craving.
sentences.zh: 我们在研究中使用了这些模型，基本上，如果你保持专注，你就会得到一个误差项，意味着我学到了：嘿，这些并不像预期的那么好，
然后我对那种行为感到幻灭。

sentences.en: So when we start looking at the core mechanism and start asking, how can we leverage the strength of the brain?
sentences.zh: 所以它可以是某种食物，可以是食物的量，可以是香烟，只需要一个人在做某种行为时真正保持专注10到15次，

sentences.en: The way that works is that our brain is going to keep doing things that are rewarding, and it's going to stop doing things that are not rewarding.
sentences.zh: 如果它没有回报，那么这种回报价值就会降至零以下。

sentences.en: And the only variable that's needed for that is awareness.
sentences.zh: 这就是这个过程的第二步。

sentences.en: And this goes back to the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为“培养幻灭感”。

sentences.en: These two researchers, Raskorla and Wagner, came up with these reinforcement learning models.
sentences.zh: 它不会改变食物的味道，特别是在我们进食量没有过度放纵时，但它确实能帮助我们在吃饱时更容易地停下来。

sentences.en: And they're still at play today.
sentences.zh: Judd 解决渴望过程的第三步是，你越关注自己的感觉，

sentences.en: We use these in our studies, where basically, if you pay attention, you're going to get an error term, meaning I learn, hey, these are not as good as expected,
sentences.zh: 你就越有可能发现他所说的比你渴望的东西“更大、更好”的替代品。

sentences.en: and I become disenchanted with that behavior.
sentences.zh: 这就是发生在 Judd 身上的事。

sentences.en: So it could be a type of food, it could be an amount of food, it could be cigarettes, and it takes only 10 to 15 times of somebody really paying attention when they do a behavior,
sentences.zh: 软糖在他生活中被更好的东西取代了。

sentences.en: if it's not rewarding, for that reward value to drop below zero.
So that's the second step in this process.
sentences.zh: 我今天早上还吃了一些。

sentences.en: It doesn't change the taste of food, especially when we are eating in amounts that are not overindulging, but it can actually help us much more easily stop when we're full.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，蓝莓是作为甜点最好的选择。

sentences.en: The third step in Judd's process to address cravings is that the more you pay attention to your sensations,
the more likely it is you will discover what he calls bigger and better alternatives to the things you crave.
sentences.zh: 当你咬它们时，它们有一种很好的口感。
它们还有这种间歇性强化的特性。

sentences.en: Gummy worms have been replaced in his life by something better.
sentences.zh: 所以你永远不知道一颗蓝莓会有多甜，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm smiling just thinking about them.
sentences.zh: 一颗可能比另一颗稍微甜一点。

sentences.en: So for me, blueberries are the biggest, bestest offer in terms of like a sweet treat.
sentences.zh: 但当你吃它们时，它们会让你不断感到惊喜。
蓝莓的好处是，对我来说，它们有完美的甜度，我不会渴望下一颗或下一品脱。

sentences.en: They've got this, you know, a nice texture when you bite into them.
sentences.zh: 我们家现在确实有一些软糖，是我妻子的家人给我们的。

sentences.en: They also have this intermittent reinforcement property.
sentences.zh: 我甚至一点兴趣都没有。

sentences.en: So you never know how sweet a blueberry is going to be, right?
One might be slightly sweeter than another.
Another might be a little more tart.

sentences.zh: 让我们回到 Jackie 的故事，你的那位多年来一直与她所谓的“渴望怪兽”作斗争的病人。

sentences.en: But they kind of keep you constantly surprised when you're eating them.
sentences.zh: 她发现好奇心和友善确实改变了她的饮食习惯。

sentences.en: And the nice thing about blueberries is, for me, they have this perfect amount of sweetness where I'm not craving the next one or the next pint.
We actually, and this is true, we have some gummy things in our house right now that my wife's family member gave to us.
sentences.zh: Jackie 和她妈妈的关系很复杂，事实上，她确实从她妈妈那里学到了一些饮食规则。
她刚从她妈妈那里回来，正如她所描述的，又是一次糟糕的旅行。

sentences.en: She doesn't even ask me anymore.

sentences.zh: 那么，让我们回到杰姬的故事上来，她就是你那位多年来一直在与她所称的“渴望怪兽”作斗争的病人。

sentences.en: So let's return to the story of Jackie, your patient who wrestled for years with what she called the craving monster.
sentences.zh: 她发现好奇心和善意确实改变了她的饮食习惯。

sentences.en: She found that curiosity and kindness really did transform her eating habits.
sentences.zh: 贾德，给我讲讲她的故事吧。

sentences.en: So Jackie had a complicated relationship with her mom and, you know, had learned some of these eating rules from her mom, in fact.
sentences.zh: 所以杰琪和她妈妈的关系很复杂，而且，你知道的，事实上她从她妈妈那里学到了一些这样的饮食规矩。

sentences.en: And she had just come from visiting her mom, as she described it, yet another horrible trip.
sentences.zh: 正如她所描述的，她刚去看望了她妈妈，那又是一次糟糕透顶的旅行。
两人之间并没有建立起联系。

sentences.en: And so she used to be in the habit of going to a certain grocery store and sitting in the parking lot, listening to loud music and just binging and binging.
sentences.zh: 所以她过去习惯去某家杂货店，坐在停车场里，听着大声的音乐，不停地暴饮暴食。

sentences.en: So she sat in her car and she said, it didn't make the upset go away.
sentences.zh: 于是她坐在车里，她说，这并没有让那种心烦意乱消失。

sentences.en: I still felt really upset and hurt with relation to her interaction with her mom.
sentences.zh: 关于她与母亲的互动，我仍然感到非常难过和受伤。

sentences.en: She said, I just bawled my eyes out in the car.
sentences.zh: 她说，我在车里哭得稀里哗啦。

sentences.en: Here's where it gets really interesting.
She said she allowed the craving monster to get in the car with her instead of ignoring it or resisting it or fighting with it.
sentences.zh: 她说她允许那个“渴望怪兽”和她一起坐在车里，而不是无视它、抗拒它或与它对抗。

sentences.en: So she simply noticed what the craving for Chinese food felt like.
sentences.zh: 所以她只是单纯地观察那种对中餐的渴望是什么感觉。

sentences.en: She could already taste that magic combination of sweet and salty.
sentences.zh: 她已经能尝到那种甜咸交织的神奇滋味了。

sentences.en: And she investigated how it felt, how that craving felt in her body, asking exactly what she was feeling and noting the sensations.
sentences.zh: 她探究了那种感觉，探究了那种渴望在身体里的感觉，精准地询问自己感受到了什么，并记录下这些身体反应。

sentences.en: And then she had this moment of revelation.
sentences.zh: 然后她有了一个顿悟的时刻。

sentences.en: She put it, I went into the grocery store and each time I picked something up, I asked myself, how am I going to feel if I eat this?
sentences.zh: 她是这样描述的：我走进杂货店，每拿起一样东西，我就问自己，如果我吃了这个，我会是什么感觉？

sentences.en: And she gave herself permission to binge if she wanted to.
sentences.zh: 她还允许自己如果想暴饮暴食的话，随时可以。

sentences.en: And here's what she walked out of the store with, some avocados and spinach.
sentences.zh: 而她最后从店里走出来时，只买了些牛油果和菠菜。

sentences.en: And she said she was laughing like a lunatic as she drove out of the parking lot because it was her first taste of freedom as an adult.
sentences.zh: 她说她开车离开停车场时笑得像个疯子，因为那是她成年后第一次尝到自由的滋味。

sentences.en: And she said, I don't have to be scared of the craving.
sentences.zh: 她说，我不必再害怕这种渴望了。

sentences.en: The craving monster is so real for so many people.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，“渴望怪兽”是真实存在的。

sentences.en: But she said, I see you.
There was a lot of fear with her with regard to the craving monster.
sentences.zh: 她曾经对这个“渴望怪兽”怀有极大的恐惧。

sentences.en: And she said the fear wasn't there anymore.
sentences.zh: 而她说，那种恐惧已经消失了。

sentences.en: Judson Brewer works at the School of Public Health and Psychiatry in the medical school at Brown University.
sentences.zh: 贾德森·布鲁尔（Judson Brewer）在布朗大学医学院的公共卫生与精神病学系工作。

sentences.en: He's the author of The Hunger Habit, Why We Eat When We're Not Hungry and How to Stop,
sentences.zh: 他是《饥饿习惯：为什么我们不饿时也会吃，以及如何停止》（The Hunger Habit, Why We Eat When We're Not Hungry and How to Stop）一书的作者，

sentences.en: and The Craving Mind, From Cigarettes to Smartphones to Love, Why We Get Hooked and How We Can Break Bad Habits.
sentences.zh: 也是《渴望的头脑：从香烟到智能手机再到爱情，为什么我们会上瘾以及如何打破坏习惯》（The Craving Mind, From Cigarettes to Smartphones to Love, Why We Get Hooked and How We Can Break Bad Habits）的作者。

sentences.zh: 贾德，非常感谢你今天参加《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）节目。
